thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: cache-sphere authz API returning 5xx for service account validation (rate-limiter reads failing) — current 5m error rate 78% — paging oncall
Asha (oncall): acknowledged, jumping in. tagging @Ben for infra help.
Asha (oncall): what region/paths?
ops-bot: Observed endpoints: https://api.cachesphere.net/auth/validate (eu-west-1, us-east-1), 502/503 cluster errors. Recent deploy? no deploys from CacheSphere reported in last 24h per vendor status page.
Ben (eng-sre): seeing a spike in our 429s from the rate-limiter metrics. Queries to the cache auth path are timing out, our middleware falls back to cache-miss behaviour which increments token lookups and rejects when quota unknown.
Asha (oncall): estimated customer impact: app-level 4xxs for auth-protected endpoints, some search and embedding requests failing with 401/429. Maria, any customer reports?
Maria (support): several customers pinged with 429s and "unable to verify token" errors. ElasticSearch of support tags: ~12 customers in EU, a couple large PLG accounts. Escalating to CS SOC.
Carlos (infra): Can we flip the rate-limiter to local fallback mode? Runbook section: https://runbooks.redwood/caching/remote-auth-fallback
Asha (oncall): executing toggle: `POST /admin/flags` body `{ "rate_limiter.remote_auth": false }` — doing a dry-toggle to local-check only for 30m.
Asha (oncall): curl command I ran:
```
curl -X POST "https://console.internal/admin/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"rate_limiter.remote_auth":false}'
```
ops-bot: flag applied: rate_limiter.remote_auth=false, scope=service, initiated_by=Asha, request_id=rb-9fa2
Ben (eng-sre): confirming: new behavior will short-circuit to local token cache and treat unknown tokens as soft-deny with extended retry window — lowers rejected calls immediately but may increase allowance for stale tokens.
Asha (oncall): monitoring token-lookup 5xx -> dropped from 70% -> 12% within 45s of toggle. 429 rate for clients dropping from 18% -> 3% in same window.
Maria (support): telling affected customers we've put a mitigation in place and are monitoring; will send follow-ups if anything changes.
Ben (eng-sre): ok next: open temporary circuit-breaker for outgoing calls to CacheSphere auth endpoints in our egress proxy to fail fast (reduce tail latencies). Carlos can you push the proxy rule?
Carlos (infra): applying egress deny to cachesphere auth path, adding 10s timeout and fail-fast config. Pushing ACL in 2m.
Carlos (infra): pushed. Logs show outbound to cachesphere auth endpoints failing fast now. Upstream error budget preserved.
Asha (oncall): PID: created incident ticket #INC-2026-3024, severity P2, notes: CacheSphere authz 5xx causing rate-limiter failures, mitigated by local fallback and egress circuit-breaker.
ops-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by Asha (oncall) — escalation set to Ben after 25m.
Ben (eng-sre): starting a temporary rollback of our remote-token-refresh job to avoid hitting vendor throttles. `systemctl stop remote-token-refresh` on rate-limiter fleet.
Asha (oncall): confirm stopping job across all pods? Ben: yes, rolling stop via k8s job pause.
Ben (eng-sre): done. packet logs: sample HTTP 502 from cachesphere: `{"error":"upstream_error","code":502}` attached.
Asha (oncall): can we quantify affected request volume? ops-bot: approx 4.2k req/min to auth endpoint pre-incident, dropped to 180 req/min after mitigations.
Maria (support): we've notified top 5 affected customers individually. One large customer reported degraded latency for chat features but accepts mitigation.
Ben (eng-sre): vendor status shows partial outage: https://status.cachesphere.net/incidents/9981 — message: "Experiencing elevated 5xx rates on token validation endpoints due to DB failover". ETA unknown.
Asha (oncall): plan: 1) keep local fallback flag for 2 hours, 2) keep egress circuit-breaker for auth path, 3) resume remote-token-refresh only when vendor clears and we see <1% 5xx for 15m, 4) schedule post-incident review. Anyone disagree?
Carlos (infra): agree. Also recommend increasing local token cache TTL by +30s to reduce backend lookups; will patch config in staging then rollout.
Ben (eng-sre): I'll prepare a rollback plan in case local cache causes token drift issues. Also collect comparison of false accept rate pre/post toggle.
Maria (support): I'll prepare customer comms template and send update in 30m.
Asha (oncall): handing off to Ben for long-running mitigation and vendor coordination. Ben — you're the lead for the next shift.
Ben (eng-sre): ack taking lead. Please ping me if anything spikes. I'll update thread with vendor contact and timeline.
ops-bot: Handoff recorded: from=Asha to=Ben at=1791234785
Ben (eng-sre): long-term: propose adding a short-circuit cache (local LRU) specifically for rate-limiter token checks with a health-check flip to avoid vendor dependency. Raising RFC after the incident.
Asha (oncall): great, thanks everyone. leaving notes in the ticket and adding list of playbook changes.
Maria (support): I'll close customer-facing thread after vendor confirms fix or we revert toggles.
ops-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> watchers=40 -> severity=P2 -> incident_ticket=INC-2026-3024
Ben (eng-sre): last check: cachesphere 5xx at 9% now (was 78%), vendor says DB failover in progress. Continue monitoring.
Asha (oncall): signing off from oncall, handoff complete.
Ben (eng-sre): continuing watch. will post final update and retrospective link once incident is resolved.
ops-bot: NOTE: please run the post-incident checklist: https://runbooks.redwood/postmortem-checklist
